source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. Crossref independently confirmed titles, authorship scope, dates, and exact DOI records for persistent data structures, atomic snapshots, MVCC, SI definitions/anomalies, serializability, SSI, and the PostgreSQL implementation paper; this check exposed and corrected an initially wrong VLDB DOI before review. Current PostgreSQL 18 MVCC and isolation documentation and current Linux kernel RCU documentation resolved directly and support the scoped product/mechanism claims. Scholarly DOI landing behavior varies by publisher, so metadata was checked through Crossref and institutional primary copies where needed. Claims are paraphrased and no inaccessible quotation is used.

numerical_recomputation.notes: The output validates the finite write-skew model only. It is not a PostgreSQL execution, a complete SSI algorithm, a durability protocol, or evidence about every SI implementation.

evidence: Path-copying induction preserves every old immutable subtree and replaces only the root-to-change path, yielding one functional update without changing the old root.
Release publication followed by acquire discovery orders complete initialization before reader traversal, subject to atomic root and lifetime assumptions.
The on-call history has T_A to-rw T_B and T_B to-rw T_A; the cycle excludes a serial order even though write sets are disjoint.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: These are reusable proof obligations, not mechanized proofs of a concrete persistent tree, compiler memory model, MVCC engine, SSI implementation, RCU implementation, or filesystem.

evidence: Every published root is completely initialized and transitively immutable; all related roots become visible through one atomic commit boundary.
Each transaction applies one declared visibility rule, hides aborted/uncommitted versions, reads its own writes, and validates every dependency required by the claimed isolation level.
Every retired version remains allocated until all reader, replica, recovery, backup, stream, rollback, and audit obligations pass their corresponding horizons.

evidence: The persistent-structure proof uses immutability plus induction from changed leaf to new root and explicitly covers private failure before publication.
The publication proof names release/acquire synchronization, one atomic root, transitively complete construction, and independent lifetime protection.
The SI anomaly proof identifies both anti-dependencies and the cycle; the reclamation proof requires announcement/load ordering and a grace condition for every reader that could reach a retired root.
proof_review.notes: Review found no inference from stable reads to serializability, from persistent data to crash durability, from garbage collection to bounded retention, or from one root swap to cross-system consistency.
